title: Piper PA-28-161 Warrior II — Emergency Procedures (independently worded)
description: Emergency procedures for the Piper PA-28-161 Warrior II with Lycoming O-320 engine. Memory items are marked. No airspeeds, power settings, fuel quantities, or other numerical limits are stated — those must come from the specific aircraft's POH. This file does not replace formal emergency training. Verify all procedures against the actual aircraft POH before flight.

source.notes: No manufacturer document was consulted or copied. This file was authored from general familiarity with the PA-28-161 type. Numerical limitations are deliberately absent and must be supplied from the aircraft's own POH.

known_issues.description: Contains no airspeeds, power settings, fuel quantities or other limitations — must come from aircraft POH.
Equipment variations exist across this model/variant. Verify items against the specific aircraft before use.

rights.notes: Manufacturer POH remains under copyright. This file does not reproduce its wording or selection of items.

sections.title: Engine Failure on Takeoff Roll (Before Lift-Off)

items.text: Throttle
Brakes
items.response: APPLY FIRMLY TO STOP ON REMAINING RUNWAY

items.text: Mixture
Magneto / ignition switch
Master switch
If unable to stop on runway, steer to minimize hazard; avoid populated areas and fuel sources
Airspeed
items.response: BEST GLIDE — ESTABLISH IMMEDIATELY PER POH

items.text: Do not attempt to turn back to the runway at low altitude. Land approximately straight ahead or with small heading changes to avoid obstacles.
Landing area — select best available surface ahead within the glide
Throttle
Mixture
items.response: IDLE CUT-OFF when landing is assured

items.text: Ignition switch
Master switch
Airspeed
items.response: BEST GLIDE PER POH — ESTABLISH IMMEDIATELY

items.text: Landing area — identify best suitable field or airport within gliding range
Fuel selector
items.response: BOTH — confirm handle fully seated in detent

items.text: Mixture
Carburetor heat
items.response: ON — apply to clear possible carburetor ice

items.text: Magnetos — cycle LEFT, then RIGHT, then BOTH
items.response: CHECK FOR DEAD MAGNETO; RETURN TO BOTH OR OPERATING POSITION

items.text: Primer
Throttle — attempt restart if propeller is windmilling
Transponder
Mayday call — current frequency or 121.5 MHz
If restart not achieved, commit to forced landing — do not delay the transition to forced landing procedure
Mixture
items.response: IDLE CUT-OFF — cut fuel to engine immediately

items.text: Fuel selector
Throttle
items.response: FULL OPEN — help exhaust residual fuel from the system

items.text: Master switch
Cabin heat and all air vents
items.response: CLOSE ALL — prevent fumes and smoke from entering cabin

items.text: Airspeed — increase as practical to aid in extinguishing flames
Land immediately at the nearest suitable area — do not delay to troubleshoot
Throttle — advance briefly to full to draw flames back into the engine through the induction system
Mixture
Fuel selector
Magneto / ignition switch
Master switch
Evacuate the aircraft immediately; move well clear upwind
Use fire extinguisher only if the fire can be safely attacked without entering the hazard zone
Master switch
items.response: OFF — remove electrical power from all circuits

items.text: Avionics master
All individual switches
Cabin vents
items.response: OPEN — ventilate to clear smoke from cockpit

items.text: If fire has subsided — master switch ON; restore switches one at a time to identify faulty circuit; leave faulty circuit OFF
items.response: FAULTY CIRCUIT ISOLATED AND LEFT OFF

items.text: Transponder — squawk 7700 if avionics are restored
Land as soon as practicable — do not delay landing after any cockpit fire or smoke event
Oil pressure indication
items.response: CONFIRM — distinguish gradual decline from sudden loss

items.text: Oil temperature
items.response: MONITOR — rising temperature with falling pressure confirms oil system distress

items.text: Power
items.response: REDUCE TO MINIMUM REQUIRED; PLAN IMMEDIATE LANDING

items.text: Landing area — identify nearest suitable airport or field; begin descending toward it
Mayday call — advise ATC of situation
items.response: DECLARED ON CURRENT FREQUENCY OR 121.5 MHz

items.text: An engine with no oil pressure can seize without warning. Do not continue flight or delay landing.
Recognition — unexplained RPM loss, rough running, or power loss; particularly in visible moisture or suspect temperature range
Carburetor heat
items.response: FULL HOT — apply immediately; do not cycle on and off

items.text: Engine response — expect initial further RPM drop as ice melts; smooth return of RPM and power confirms ice was present
Carburetor heat — leave ON until icing conditions are exited and normal operation is confirmed
If engine does not recover, declare emergency and initiate forced landing without delay
Airspeed
items.response: BEST GLIDE PER POH — ESTABLISH AND MAINTAIN

items.text: Landing area — select largest available flat surface, preferably into wind; avoid terrain, wires, and populated areas
Mayday call — position, altitude, souls on board, intentions
items.response: TRANSMITTED ON CURRENT FREQUENCY OR 121.5 MHz

items.text: Transponder
Approach — fly a recognizable pattern to the chosen field; preserve altitude margin; do not undershoot
Flaps — deploy as needed to manage touchdown point and energy
Fuel selector — OFF on short final
Mixture — IDLE CUT-OFF on short final
Magneto / ignition switch — OFF on short final
Master switch — OFF on short final
Doors — unlatch before touchdown to prevent jamming and ease evacuation
Touch down at minimum sink rate; aim for far end of available landing area to maximize rollout distance
